ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that the functional relationship between $y$ and $x$ is as illustrated. Specifically, when $x \geq 0$, $y = x$; when $x < 0$, $y = -2x + 1$. Then, what is the range of $x$ when the function value $y > 3$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Substitute $y=3$ into $y=x$, then $x=3$.\\
Substitute $y=3$ into $y=-2x+1$ to get, $3=-2x+1$, solving this gives $x=-1$.\\
Therefore, the points of intersection between the line $y=3$ and the graph of the function are $(3,3)$ and $(-1,3)$.\\
Observing the graph, when the function value $y>3$, the range of $x$ is $x<-1$ or $x>3$,\\
thus, the answer is: $\boxed{x \in (-\infty, -1) \cup (3, +\infty)}$.
